10. Mr Alaluddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party argued that this revisional application is not maintainable provided under section 17 of the Family Courts Ordinance, since provision of sub-section 2 of section 17 appeal shall lie from a judgment and decree or order of a family court to the District Judge and since this is a special provision and law specifically mentioned that any order of the Family Court is appealable order and, as such, the revisional application provide under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not sustainable. He relying upon the decision of the case of Md Firofid Islam (Firop vs Mossamat Zahanara Akter, reported in 5 MLR 23 = 52 DLR 107. 

 13. In the instant case it is found that the petitioner without invoking the provision of appeal provided under section 17 of the Family Court Ordinance filed this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of the Civil Procedure. Sub-section 1 of section 17 of the Family Court Ordinance provides that subject to the provision of sub-section 2 an appeal shall lie for a judgment, decree or order of a Family Court to the court of District Judge. Since this is a special law and the law specifically provided that any judgment, decree or order of the Family Court the aggrieved party should prefer appeal to the District Judge. This proposition also supported by the decision of the case of Md Firojul Islam (Firoj) vs Mosammat Zahanara Akter, reported in 5 MLR 23 = 52 DLR 107. Wherein principle laid down as under:
